reason: Playwright's frameLocator() with no selector searches every frame in the page for its chain, the main frame included, and fails when the chain matches in more than one frame. Strider enters a frame only by its iframe element (page.frame(iframe)), so there is no search across frames to assert on. The matrix's Page.frameLocator row says has, but it maps to the iframe-element form only; no row names the selector-less form, which is the missing feature

Playwright's frameLocator() with no selector searches every frame in the page, and does not wait on a frame that never finishes loading, so these tests check a click, a visibility and a count while a sibling iframe is stalled. Strider has no search across frames to stall, and naming the frame would not exercise that. Missing: the selector-less frame locator (see the other entries under this matrix row)

Playwright's frameLocator() with no selector resolves each operand of an `or` from the frame the search found: LO-043's operand is built on `page`, which has no button in the main frame, and LO-044's is a second `frameLocator('#f')` from the main frame, which has no #f. Both only find their element because the search starts the operand in the frame it found. Strider enters a frame only by its iframe element, so naming the frame makes both operands one chain in one frame and asserts nothing about that resolution. Missing: the selector-less frame locator (see the other entries under this matrix row; the matrix's Page.frameLocator row says has, but it maps to the iframe-element form only, and no row names the selector-less form)

Playwright rejects first(), last(), and nth() on frameLocator(), its frame locator with no selector. Strider's frame locator has none of those methods: the iframe is selected on its element locator before the frame is entered (method-framelocator-first and the nth row), so there is no call to reject
